registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered on his instruction to close every closable gap, before any run of this test
hypothesis: The app's GDP forecast rule (AR on quarterly real GDP growth, lag 0-4 by BIC, all data to then), fitted at each origin on the series as it stood in that month's OECD Main Economic Indicators edition, has a lower RMSE than the historical mean computed on the same edition, one and four quarters ahead, scored against each quarter's first published figure. Every OECD member with saved editions, pooled.
knownLimits: Same model rule, benchmark, horizons and pass mark as gdp_forecast_realtime (US and euro area); this test widens the same question to the OECD members.
An edition is taken as out on the first day of its month: the OECD gives the month, not the day.
The OECD editions start in February 1999, so the early origins have fewer past editions behind them; origins start in 2008.
Euro area members count separately (each has its own GDP), unlike the shared policy rate in other tests.
